examples.en: I cried all night, so my eyes are puffy.
Your face looks puffy; maybe you couldn't sleep.
I woke up in the morning with a puffy face and was startled.

examples.ko: 라면을 먹고 자면 다음 날 얼굴이 부석부석한 것 같아요.
examples.en: If I eat ramyeon and go to bed, my face seems puffy the next day.

examples.ko: 눈이 부석부석하면 찬 수건을 올려 보세요.
examples.en: If your eyes are puffy, try putting a cold towel on them.

examples.ko: 부석부석한 얼굴에 팩을 붙이고 잠깐 쉬었어요.
examples.en: I put a face mask on my puffy face and rested for a bit.

explain: 잠을 못 자거나 울거나 짜게 먹은 뒤에 얼굴이나 눈이 핏기 없이 부어 보일 때 써요. '푸석푸석하다'(거칠고 윤기가 없다)와 소리가 비슷해서 헷갈리기 쉬워요. 보통 '얼굴', '눈'과 함께 써요.

phrases.en: I went to work with a puffy face.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-한'을 붙여서 명사를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -한 lets it modify a noun.

phrases.example: 어제 못 잤는지 눈이 부석부석해 보여요.
phrases.en: Your eyes look puffy, maybe because you didn't sleep yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이 그렇게 보인다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something looks that way.

phrases.example: 라면을 먹고 잤더니 아침에 얼굴이 부석부석해졌어요.
phrases.en: I ate ramen and slept, so my face got puffy in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-해지다'는 상태가 변했다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: -해지다 shows a change of state.

explain_en: It describes a face or eyes that look swollen and pale, for example after missing sleep, crying or eating salty food. It sounds similar to '푸석푸석하다' (rough and dull), so it is easy to mix up. It is usually used with '얼굴' (face) and '눈' (eyes).

en: to be dotted with red; to be streaked with red

examples.en: The leaves have turned, so the mountain is dotted with red all over.
The mosquito bites are red and itchy.
Children run around among the red-dotted flower beds.
Red blotches came up on my face, so I went to a dermatologist.

examples.ko: 저녁 노을 때문에 바다가 불긋불긋해 보였어요.
examples.en: The sea looked patchy red because of the sunset.
The apples are ripening with red patches.

explain: '불긋불긋'은 부사이고 이 말은 형용사라서 '불긋불긋한 단풍'처럼 뒤의 말을 꾸밀 수 있어요. 여러 색이 섞이면 '울긋불긋하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: As the weather got cold, the leaves turned reddish.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어지다'를 붙여서 색이 변해 간다는 뜻을 만들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -아/어지다 shows the color is changing.

phrases.en: The park is colorful with autumn leaves.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 색이 섞여 있을 때는 '불긋불긋하다' 대신 이 말을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this instead of 불긋불긋하다 when many colors are mixed.

phrases.example: 이제 모기에 물린 자리가 불긋불긋하지 않아요.
phrases.en: The mosquito bite is not red and spotty anymore.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-지 않다'를 붙여 부정할 때 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form using -지 않다.

explain_en: '불긋불긋' is an adverb, while this word is an adjective, so you can say '불긋불긋한 단풍' to modify a noun. When several colors are mixed, use '울긋불긋하다'.

examples.en: I bought a bikini for my summer vacation.

examples.ko: 그녀는 파란 비키니를 입고 바다로 갔어요.
examples.en: She went to the sea wearing a blue bikini.
I wore a thin shirt over my bikini.
I put the bikini in my bag.
This shop sells bikinis too.
The bikini got too small, so I have to buy a new one.

explain: 수영복은 '수영복'이 가장 일반적이고, '비키니'는 위아래가 나뉜 수영복만 가리켜요. 한 벌로 된 수영복은 보통 '원피스 수영복'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I took photos in a bikini at the beach.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷을 입는 동사 '입다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with the clothing verb 입다.

phrases.example: 작년에 산 비키니 수영복이 아직 새것 같아요.
phrases.en: The bikini swimsuit I bought last year still looks new.
phrases.nuance_ko: '수영복' 앞에 붙여서 어떤 수영복인지 분명하게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Putting it before 수영복 makes clear which type of swimsuit.

phrases.en: I find a two-piece swimsuit more comfortable than a bikini.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위아래가 나뉜 수영복을 조금 더 넓게 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broader name for swimsuits with separate top and bottom.

explain_en: 수영복 is the general word for swimwear, while 비키니 means only the two-piece kind. A one-piece suit is usually called '원피스 수영복'.

examples.en: I put on lotion after washing up.
I packed my toiletries and went on a trip.
There are two washbasins in the bathroom.
In the morning I wash up and brush my teeth.
The hotel has toiletries prepared.

examples.ko: 세면할 때 물을 오래 틀어 두지 마세요.
examples.en: Do not leave the water running long when washing up.

explain: 혼자서는 잘 안 쓰고 '세면대', '세면도구' 같은 말에서 많이 봐요. 일상에서는 '세면했어요'보다 '세수했어요'라고 말해요. '세면'은 안내문이나 설명서에 나오는 조금 격식 있는 말이에요.

phrases.en: I wash my hands at the sink.
phrases.nuance_ko: 화장실에서 씻는 곳을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is the washbasin in a bathroom.

phrases.en: I put my toiletries in my bag.
phrases.nuance_ko: 칫솔, 비누처럼 씻을 때 쓰는 물건을 모두 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It covers items for washing, such as a toothbrush or soap.

explain_en: Formal; mostly in compounds like washstand (세면대) It rarely stands alone and appears in words like '세면대' and '세면도구'. In daily speech people say '세수했어요' rather than '세면했어요'. '세면' is a slightly formal word found in notices and manuals.

examples.en: At the bathhouse I got into the warm bath to loosen up.
I tried going back and forth between the hot and cold baths.

examples.ko: 온탕은 너무 뜨거워서 오래 못 있겠어요.
examples.en: The hot bath is so hot that I can't stay long.
The kids splashed around in the warm bath.

examples.ko: 피곤할 때는 온탕에 십 분쯤 몸을 담가요.
examples.en: When I'm tired, I soak in the warm bath for about ten minutes.

examples.ko: 이 사우나는 온탕이 두 개나 있어요.
examples.en: This sauna has as many as two hot baths.

explain: 대중목욕탕에서 따뜻한 물이 있는 탕을 말해요. 반대말은 '냉탕'이고, 보통 두 탕을 번갈아 이용해요. 집 욕조의 따뜻한 물에는 잘 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: Soaking in the hot bath relieves my tiredness.
phrases.nuance_ko: 따뜻한 물에 몸을 푹 넣는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes sinking the body into warm water.
phrases.en_equiv: to soak in the hot bath

phrases.en: After the hot bath I got into the cold bath.
phrases.nuance_ko: 온탕의 반대말로, 찬물이 있는 탕이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 온탕: the bath with cold water.

phrases.en: I was cold, so I got into the hot bath first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 목욕탕에서 따뜻한 탕으로 들어가는 동작을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the action of getting into the warm bath at a public bathhouse.
phrases.en_equiv: to get into the hot bath

explain_en: It refers to the pool with warm water in a public bathhouse. The opposite is '냉탕', and people often alternate between the two. It is not typically used for warm water in a home bathtub.

examples.ko: 항아리 주둥이가 좁아서 물을 붓기 어려워요.
examples.en: The jar's mouth is narrow, so it's hard to pour water in.
The bird pecked at the insect with its beak.

examples.ko: 강아지가 주둥이를 내 손에 갖다 댔어요.
examples.en: The puppy put its snout against my hand.
Steam is rising from the spout of the kettle.

examples.ko: 주둥이 끝이 뾰족한 새를 본 적 있어요?
examples.en: Have you ever seen a bird with a pointed beak?

examples.ko: 병 주둥이를 입에 대고 마시지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't drink with your mouth on the bottle's opening.

explain: 새나 동물의 입 부분, 그리고 병이나 주전자처럼 좁게 튀어나온 입구를 가리킬 때 써요. 사람의 입에 쓰면 낮춰 부르는 말이라 무례하게 들리니 보통은 '입'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 병 주둥이가 좁아서 손이 안 들어가요.
phrases.en: The bottle's mouth is narrow, so my hand won't fit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병이나 주전자의 좁은 입구를 말할 때 써요. 이럴 때는 무례하지 않아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the narrow opening of a bottle or kettle; not rude in this use.

phrases.example: 저 새는 주둥이가 길어서 쉽게 알아봐요.
phrases.en: That bird has a long beak, so it's easy to recognize.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새나 동물의 생김새를 설명할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the shape of a bird's or animal's mouth.

phrases.en: My younger sibling laughed with their mouth wide open.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람 입에는 '주둥이' 대신 '입'을 써야 예의 바르게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: For people, use '입' instead of '주둥이' to sound polite.

explain_en: It is used for the mouth part of birds and animals, and for the narrow opening or spout of bottles and kettles. Using it for a person's mouth sounds rude and belittling, so people normally say '입'.

examples.en: I got hemorrhoids from sitting and working for a long time.
I had hemorrhoid surgery and rested for a week.
My hemorrhoids got worse, so I went to the hospital.
If you have constipation, you easily get hemorrhoids.

examples.ko: 아버지가 치질 때문에 오래 앉아 있기 힘들어하세요.
examples.en: My father has a hard time sitting for long because of hemorrhoids.

examples.ko: 치질은 부끄러워하지 말고 빨리 치료받아야 해요.
examples.en: Don't be embarrassed about hemorrhoids; get treated quickly.

explain: '양치질'의 '치질' 부분과 모양이 비슷해서 헷갈리기 쉽지만 전혀 다른 말이에요. 이를 닦는 건 '양치질', 이건 항문의 병이에요. '치질에 걸리다/치질이 생기다'처럼 써요.

phrases.example: 오래 앉아 있으면 치질에 걸릴 수 있어요.
phrases.en: If you sit for a long time, you can get hemorrhoids.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병에 걸린다는 뜻으로 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The phrase for catching an illness.

phrases.en: I had bad constipation and developed hemorrhoids.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸에 증상이 나타났다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Feels like the condition appeared in the body.

phrases.en: The hemorrhoid surgery ended sooner than I expected.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병을 치료하는 방법으로 수술을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about surgery as a treatment for the condition.

explain_en: It looks like the last part of '양치질', so it is easy to mix up, but they are unrelated. Brushing teeth is '양치질', while this is a condition of the anus. You say '치질에 걸리다' or '치질이 생기다'.

en: to burp; to belch; to eruct

examples.en: The baby burped after drinking milk.
I burp often when I drink soda.
It is rude to burp during a meal.

examples.ko: 아기가 트림할 때까지 등을 두드려 주세요.
examples.en: Pat the baby's back until the baby burps.
After I burped, my stomach felt better.
I was embarrassed because I burped in front of a friend.

explain: 한국에서는 어른이 사람들 앞에서 트림하면 예의 없다고 느끼는 경우가 많아요. 반대로 아기는 우유를 먹은 뒤에 트림을 시켜 줘야 해서 '트림시키다'라는 말을 써요. '트림을 하다'라고 띄어 써도 뜻이 같아요.

phrases.en: I burped after eating and felt embarrassed.
phrases.nuance_ko: '트림하다'와 뜻이 같고, 말할 때는 이렇게 띄어서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '트림하다'; this spaced form is very common in speech.

phrases.en: I hold the baby and pat its back to make it burp.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아기가 트림하게 도와줄 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means helping a baby to burp, rather than burping yourself.

phrases.en: I drank sparkling water and now I keep burping.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내가 일부러 하는 게 아니라 저절로 나올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the burp comes out on its own rather than on purpose.

explain_en: In Korea, burping in front of others as an adult is often seen as impolite. For babies, though, you help them burp after feeding, which is '트림시키다'. Writing '트림을 하다' with a space means the same.

examples.ko: 모기가 제 팔뚝을 여러 군데 물었어요.
examples.en: A mosquito bit my forearm in several places.
His forearms are thick and he is strong.
After I started exercising, my forearms became firm.
The nurse gave me an injection in my forearm.

examples.ko: 팔뚝 살을 빼고 싶어서 운동을 해요.
examples.en: I exercise because I want to lose arm fat.

examples.ko: 팔뚝에 큰 문신이 있는 사람이 지나갔어요.
examples.en: A person with a big tattoo on the forearm walked by.

explain: 팔꿈치와 손목 사이, 또는 어깨와 팔꿈치 사이 굵은 부분을 가리키는 일상적인 말이에요. 의학 용어로는 '아래팔', '위팔'로 나누지만 일상에서는 보통 '팔뚝' 하나로 말해요. '팔뚝 살'처럼 몸매 이야기에 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 여름이 되면 팔뚝 살이 신경 쓰여요.
phrases.en: In summer I worry about my arm fat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸매 이야기에서 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when talking about body shape.

phrases.en: I got a shot in my arm at the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원에서 주사 맞는 곳을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say where you got a shot.
phrases.en_equiv: to get a shot in the arm

phrases.en: I fell and got a bruise on my arm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다친 곳을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say where you are hurt.
phrases.en_equiv: to get a bruise on the arm

explain_en: It is an everyday word for the thick part of the arm, between elbow and wrist or between shoulder and elbow. Medical terms separate 아래팔 and 위팔, but in daily life people just say 팔뚝. It often appears in body-shape talk, like 팔뚝 살.

en: to burn; to glow; to flush

examples.en: I sat in front of the heater and my face feels hot.
After eating spicy food, my mouth felt like it was burning.
I stayed in the sun a long time and my arms feel hot.

examples.ko: 사우나에서 나오자 온몸이 후끈거리는 느낌이 들었어요.
examples.en: When I came out of the sauna, my whole body felt flushed with heat.
I was so embarrassed that even my ears felt hot, so I lowered my head.
The room is stuffy and hot, so please open the window.

explain: 더운 기운이 확 올라오는 느낌을 말해요. 얼굴이나 몸이 뜨겁다고 할 때뿐 아니라 방 안의 열기에도 쓸 수 있어요. 피부가 쓰리거나 얼얼하면서 달아오르는 느낌은 '화끈거리다'가 더 잘 맞아요.

phrases.en: The room is warm and toasty after I turned on the heater.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더운 기운이 느껴지는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a state where you feel hot air.

phrases.en: It is steaming hot inside the sauna.
phrases.nuance_ko: 열기가 계속 올라오는 느낌을 더 강하게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Stresses the feeling of heat continuously rising.

phrases.en: My arm burns because I got sunburned.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피부가 쓰리고 달아오르는 느낌에 더 잘 맞아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits better for skin that stings and feels hot.

explain_en: It describes a rush of hot air or heat coming up, and can be used for your face or body as well as the heat in a room. When skin stings or tingles while burning up, '화끈거리다' fits better.

t90.ax: I sat in front of the heater and my face feels hot.

en: showy appearance; vanity; putting on airs

examples.en: He has no skill and only puts on a show.
He's caught up in looking stylish and only wants expensive clothes.
Drop the showiness and practice from the basics.

examples.ko: 겉멋에 빠진 신인들이 많다고 선배가 말했어요.
examples.en: My senior said there are many newcomers caught up in appearances.
Showing off is obvious quickly, so be careful.

examples.ko: 사진 찍을 때 겉멋 부리지 말고 자연스럽게 웃어 보세요.
examples.en: When taking photos, don't pose too much and just smile naturally.

explain: 실속 없이 멋있어 보이려는 태도를 말해서 칭찬이 아니라 약간 부정적인 말이에요. '겉멋이 들다', '겉멋을 부리다'처럼 자주 써요.

phrases.en: These days my younger sibling has become all about looking cool.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉멋을 부리고 싶은 마음이 생겼다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means a desire to show off has taken hold.
phrases.en_equiv: to get caught up in showiness

phrases.en: Don't show off; learn the basics first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일부러 멋있어 보이려고 행동할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when someone acts on purpose to look cool.

phrases.en: That restaurant is all style and the food is not great.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉만 멋있고 속은 부족하다는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It says something looks good outside but lacks substance.

explain_en: It describes an attitude of trying to look cool without substance, so it is slightly negative rather than a compliment. It is often used as '겉멋이 들다' or '겉멋을 부리다'.

examples.en: Don't cry over such a trivial thing.

examples.ko: 고까짓 것쯤은 저도 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even I can do a little thing like that.

examples.ko: 고까짓 돈 때문에 친구랑 싸우지 말아요.
examples.en: Don't fight with your friend over a measly bit of money.

examples.ko: 고까짓 시험 하나 망쳤다고 포기하지 말아요.
examples.en: Don't give up just because you messed up one little test.
You don't need to be hurt by such petty words.
A height like that is not scary at all.

explain: '그까짓'과 같은 뜻인데, 더 작게 보고 얕잡아 보는 느낌이 강해요. 뒤에 '일, 것, 돈, 말' 같은 명사가 오고, 윗사람에게나 격식 있는 자리에서는 어울리지 않아요.

phrases.en: I don't mind not getting such a trifling amount of money.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈의 액수를 아주 작게 보고 얕잡아 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to dismiss an amount of money as trivial.

phrases.en: Don't worry about such a petty remark.
phrases.nuance_ko: 별것 아닌 말이라고 여기며 위로하거나 무시할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to brush off words as unimportant, either to comfort someone or to dismiss them.

phrases.en: A trivial task like that is done quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻은 같지만 '고까짓'보다 더 흔하고 얕잡는 느낌이 조금 약해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning but more common, with a slightly weaker tone of belittling.

explain_en: It means the same as '그까짓' but sounds even more dismissive, as if shrinking the thing down. A noun like '일', '것', '돈' or '말' follows it, and it does not suit talking to elders or formal situations.

t90.ax: Don't cry over such a trivial thing.

examples.en: There's no need to cry over such a small thing.
That little bit of money is nothing.

examples.ko: 그까짓 시험 한 번 망쳤다고 포기하지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't give up just because you messed up one measly exam.
A cold like that gets better after a day of sleep.

examples.ko: 그까짓 애들이라니요? 다들 집안에서 귀하게 큰 아이들이에요.
examples.en: What do you mean, just kids? They are all children raised with great care.
You want to cancel our plans over a little rain?

explain: 별것 아니라고 얕잡아 보는 느낌이 있어서 말투가 센 편이에요. 윗사람 앞에서 쓰면 무례하게 들릴 수 있고, 친구를 격려할 때는 가볍게 쓸 수 있어요. '그깟'으로 줄여 말하기도 하고, 뒤에 꼭 명사가 와요.

phrases.en: I'll forget a trivial thing like that quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '그까짓'의 줄임말로 말할 때 더 자주 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The shortened form of '그까짓', heard more often in speech.

phrases.example: 그까짓 것쯤은 저도 할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Even I can do a small thing like that.
phrases.nuance_ko: '것'을 붙이면 어떤 일이나 물건이 별것 아니라는 뜻이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '것' makes it mean 'that little thing' that is nothing special.

phrases.example: 그까짓 게 뭐라고 그렇게 화를 내요?
phrases.en: It's just a small thing, why are you so angry?
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 일에 크게 반응하는 사람에게 말할 때 쓰는데, 말투가 센 편이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said to someone overreacting to something small, with a rather strong tone.
phrases.en_equiv: what's the big deal about that

explain_en: Standard full form, spoken, belittles a thing near the listener. It carries a dismissive tone, so it sounds strong. It can sound rude toward someone older, but works lightly when encouraging a friend. It can be shortened to '그깟', and a noun must always follow it.

en: to be low; to be hushed

examples.en: His voice was low but firm.
The song drifted out softly.

examples.ko: 목소리가 나직해서 뒷자리에서는 잘 안 들려요.
examples.en: The voice is so low that it's hard to hear from the back seats.

examples.ko: 밤에는 말소리가 나직해야 이웃이 안 깨요.
examples.en: At night your voice has to be quiet so the neighbors don't wake up.

examples.ko: 마을 뒤에 나직한 언덕이 하나 있어요.
examples.en: There is a low hill behind the village.

examples.ko: 나직하다고 해서 힘이 없는 소리는 아니에요.
examples.en: A low voice isn't necessarily a weak one.

explain: 소리가 낮고 조용하며 차분한 느낌일 때 써요. 그냥 '낮다'와 달리 흥분하지 않은 침착한 분위기가 있어요. 소리뿐 아니라 언덕이나 지붕처럼 높이가 꽤 낮은 것에도 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: Because he spoke in a low voice, I felt at ease.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤의 명사를 꾸며 줄 때 쓰는 형태로, 목소리와 가장 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifying form, which pairs best with 'voice'.

phrases.example: 밤에 나직하게 부는 바람 소리가 좋아요.
phrases.en: I like the sound of the wind blowing softly at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게'를 붙여 동작을 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -게 lets it describe a verb.

phrases.en: His voice is always low and calm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 말소리를 설명하는 해요체 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form for describing someone's speaking voice.

explain_en: Literary; mostly for a quiet, low voice (나직한 목소리). It describes a sound that is low, quiet and calm. Unlike plain '낮다', it carries a composed, unexcited mood. Besides sounds, it can also be used for things fairly low in height, such as a hill or a roof.

t90.ax: His voice was low but firm.
